binders: An assumption that μ is a probability measure.
hypotheses: X is measurable from Ω to the Borel real line.
conclusions: LocalDef001 μ X is at most ENNReal.ofReal(B/sqrt(log 2)).

Equivalently, the infimum over all finite, nonzero extended-nonnegative-real t for which exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) is integrable and has μ-integral at most 2 is bounded above by the extended-nonnegative-real image of B/sqrt(log 2).
mathematical_definitions: Define A(μ,X) to be the set of t ∈ [0,∞] such that X is measurable, t ≠ 0, t ≠ ∞, the real-valued function ω ↦ exp((X(ω))^2/(t.toReal)^2) is μ-integrable, and ∫ exp((X(ω))^2/(t.toReal)^2) dμ(ω) ≤ 2.
LocalDef001 μ X = inf A(μ,X), with the infimum taken in the complete order ENNReal.
The almost-everywhere hypothesis means that the exceptional set on which |X(ω)| > B is μ-null.
ENNReal.ofReal(r) is the extended nonnegative real obtained from max(r,0).
The square root is the nonnegative real square root, and log is the real logarithm.
translation.proposition_plain_english: On any probability space, let X be a measurable real-valued function and let B>0. If |X| is at most B almost everywhere, then the infimum of all finite positive parameters t for which the exponential-square moment exp(X^2/t^2) is integrable and has expectation at most 2 is no greater than B/sqrt(log 2), viewed as an extended nonnegative real.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The result applies only under the probability-measure typeclass assumption on μ; no conclusion is asserted for an arbitrary unnormalized measure.
The bound on X is only μ-almost everywhere, not pointwise everywhere.
X is nevertheless required to be globally measurable as a function into the Borel real line.
The theorem assumes B>0 and does not include the endpoint case B=0.
Admissible parameters t are extended nonnegative reals but must be neither 0 nor infinity, so their real projections act as finite positive denominators.
The infimum itself may equal 0 even though 0 is excluded from the admissible set; the proposition does not assert that the infimum is attained.

If the admissible set were empty, its complete-lattice infimum would follow ENNReal's empty-infimum convention; under the stated hypotheses the claimed bound implicitly requires enough admissible parameters for the inequality to hold.

ENNReal.ofReal truncates negative real inputs to 0. Here B>0 and the standard constant sqrt(log 2) is positive, so the intended right-hand side is positive, but that positivity is not an explicit hypothesis.
No centering, zero-mean, symmetry, independence, or distributional hypothesis on X is encoded.
The conclusion concerns precisely the exponential-square threshold 2 and the normalization exp(X^2/t^2); it does not state a tail bound or any other moment estimate.
Changing X on a μ-null set does not affect the almost-everywhere bound or the integral condition, although the displayed measurability hypothesis remains explicit.
